thread:
maya: heads-up — customer reported being charged for ~2x tokens when a stream reconnect happened and a toolcall truncated the response. billing shows both partial stream and final response credited.
sanjay: ugh, this is the classic partial-stream vs committed-charge mismatch. do we have a stream_id in router logs for that session?
alex: yes — found case where router routed initial stream to cheap-v1, then after reconnect routed to highperf-v2. client retried because it got a 499 mid-stream. both sides emitted tokens.
paige: are we treating toolcalls as atomic? if a toolcall truncates we might be counting both the toolcall output + resumed generation. need to confirm billing path.
lucas: digging into billing pipeline — we currently attribute token buckets on chunk emission events from runtime. if a reconnect emits a prefix again we count it. no dedupe today.
maya: here's the minimal repro from the customer logs:```
CLIENT: open stream -> stream_id=abc123 -> got 499 mid-stream
CLIENT: retry with same payload -> server accepted -> stream resumes as new stream_id=def456
TOOLCALL: runtime emitted tool output (100 tokens) then generator emitted final (200 tokens)
BILLING: charged 300 tokens for def456 and 100 tokens for abc123
```
alex: two problems: (1) router sticky-session broke on reconnect so stream_id changed, (2) billing has no cross-stream dedupe or session correlation.
sanjay: proposal: require client to send X-Client-Stream-Id and preserve it through routing. billing can then group events by client_stream_id and only commit once a finalization event is seen.
paige: what about long-lived partial caches? some customers intentionally checkpoint partial results and re-open streams. dedupe by client_stream_id might undercount in those legitimate cases.
lucas: true. we need to distinguish intentional resume vs accidental retry. maybe a per-stream finalization flag: runtime emits stream_finalized=true when completed successfully. only then commit tokens; otherwise mark provisional. dashboards should surface provisional vs committed tokens.
maya: sounds good. low-risk: implement provisional credits that don't hit invoices until finalized. show provisional tokens in console with yellow badge and committed in green.
alex: implementation notes:
- router: pass through X-Client-Stream-Id header, fallback to generated if missing
- runtime: emit events with client_stream_id and finalized flag
- billing: on receipt of token event, write provisional rows; on finalized flip to committed and dedupe by client_stream_id+seq_range
- telemetry: new metric billing.provisional_to_committed_ratio, billing.dedupe_hits
- alert: if >1% of provisional tokens remain uncommitted after 24h, paging to eng-platform oncall
```
paige: UX: console timeline should allow expanding a request to see provisional entries, and a toggle to include provisional in usage view. for billing invoices we must exclude provisional by default.
lucas: DB note: provisional writes must be cheap — append-only table with TTL then compaction when finalized. need to ensure we can roll back provisional entries if a stream never finalizes.
sanjay: rollout plan: feature flag controlled. canary to 10% of router traffic routed to a branch that preserves client_stream_id header and emits provisional events. enable billing dedupe in read-only/monitoring mode (no invoice changes) to evaluate reconciliation.
maya: timeline? can we get a quick spike this week to add header passthrough + runtime finalized flag?
alex: I can push a small router PR today to passthrough X-Client-Stream-Id and stop rewriting session id on reconnect. runtime change requires a minor event schema bump, I'll start a changelist.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: eng-platform/router-canary -> 10% -> 1729990180
paige: while we're here, telemetry needs to tag toolcall-generated tokens separately (tool_tokens vs gen_tokens) so console can show where truncation happened.
lucas: agreed. add token_source label on events.
sanjay: owners: alex (router + runtime schema), lucas (billing changes + provisional store), paige (console UX + metrics), maya (customer comms + reconciliation).
maya: I'll draft a short note to support + CS explaining provisional tokens and that we're doing a canary.
alex: PRs: router: https://git.internal/r/router/+/1234, runtime: https://git.internal/r/runtime/+/5678 (WIP)
paige: small design question — should we show provisional tokens in quota consumption? customers hit quota ceiling on provisionals can be surprising. maybe quota should use committed only, with an opt-in preview mode for provisional.
lucas: yes use committed for quotas. provisional available in console and billing preview but not enforced.
maya: ok, sounds like a plan. quick checklist: router header passthrough, runtime finalized flag, provisional billing path, console provisional UI, telemetry metrics, canary to 10%.
sanjay: I'll write the RFC for the billing dedupe rules (seq ranges, overlaps, TTL). aim to get it reviewed tomorrow.
paige: I can mock the console badges tonight.
alex: I'll cut the router PR and ping infra for canary.
deploy-bot: router canary deployed -> 10% -> 1729990240 :shipit:
maya: monitoring queries to watch:```
- sum(billing_provisional_tokens) by service
- rate(billing_dedupe_hits[5m])
- provisional_to_committed_ratio{job="billing"}
```
paige: tagging CS and support docs as follow-ups. :eyes:
lucas: assign jira ENGPLAT-3421 for billing work, ENGPLAT-3422 for runtime event, ENGPLAT-3423 for console UX.
maya: thanks team. will update once we confirm reconciliation results from canary.
